ai.req.label: Requirement
ai.req.chatgpt_plus: ChatGPT Plus or Pro. Free does not work, and OpenAI currently does not list Go. Usage counts against the plan's limits.
ai.req.api_paid: API account with the provider with credit or a payment method, billed by usage. Chat plans such as ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro do not cover it.
ai.req.api_free_tier: API account with the provider. There is a free tier with limits; above it, usage is billed.
ai.req.local: Free. Runs on your own computer or server and needs enough memory or a graphics card.
ai.req.m365_license: Microsoft 365 Copilot licence in the organisation and approval by IT.
ai.req.cloud_contract: Cloud account with the provider (e.g. Azure, AWS or Google Cloud subscription) with the model enabled.
ai.edit.login_running: Waiting for sign-in in the browser …

ai.edit.entra_hint: Empty fields use the defaults (any work account, Microsoft Graph command line app). Your admin may have to approve the app once.

ai.panel.detail_tip: Level of detail of the answers
ai.panel.empty_text: Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, a local model or a company bot in the settings. Many services work with a single sign-in in the browser.
ai.panel.welcome: {name} is ready. Ask about OmniWrench, its tools or your systems.

ai.store.title: Where AI data is stored
ai.store.hint: Everything is stored locally in readable formats (JSON, Markdown, PNG, MP3, MP4). Media files are never encrypted.
ai.store.encrypt_hint: Encrypted data can only be opened by OmniWrench with this vault. Other programs (editor, search, backup viewers) can no longer read it, and it is lost if the vault is reset.
ai.store.move_question: Move the existing data to the new folders? ({types})
ai.access.title_app: What may assistants see of OmniWrench?
ai.access.title_tool: What may assistants see of this tool?
ai.access.hint: Applies to all assistants. Different levels per assistant can be set under "Exceptions".
ai.access.inherit_desc: Follows the setting on the "AI access" page of the main program.
ai.level.1_desc: Profile, wiki page, whether installed and connected.
ai.level.2_desc: Summaries and counts (e.g. servers, scopes, findings), no individual records.
ai.level.3_desc: Individual records such as leases, records, settings and check results.
ai.level.4_desc: Assistants may propose actions; every change must be confirmed.
ai.access.pseudo_hint: Real values are replaced by placeholders before sending. Answers are translated back locally, so you see the real values.
ai.pseudo.keep_network: Keep network structure (same network stays the same network)
ai.access.preview_hint: Values that tools mark as host or user names are replaced as well.
ai.access.exceptions_hint: A different level for single assistants, e.g. more for a local model, less for a cloud service.

ai.ask.placeholder: e.g. What stands out here? What should I check?
ai.ask.default_question: Please explain this and point out anything noticeable.
ai.ask.notice: Pseudonymization and AI access of the tool apply as configured.

ai.transcript.consent_note: Consent of all participants confirmed on {time}.
ai.model.tip.top: Best answers for difficult questions, but slower and more expensive.
ai.model.tip.balanced: Good answers at moderate cost. A sensible default.
ai.model.tip.fast: Answers quickly and costs little. Good enough for most everyday questions.
ai.model.tip.light: Smallest and cheapest variant, for simple tasks and large amounts of text.
ai.model.tip.reasoning: Works through a problem step by step before answering. Good for analyses and troubleshooting, takes longer.
ai.model.tip.code: Specialised in program code and scripts.
ai.model.tip.vision: Can also read attached images and screenshots.
ai.model.tip.free: Free of charge with this provider, usually with tight limits.
ai.model.tip.preview: Test version: may change or disappear at short notice.
ai.model.title: Choose model – {name}
ai.model.intro: The list comes directly from the provider. ★ marks the recommended model. Hover over a model for an explanation.
ai.model.show_other: Also show other models (images, speech, embeddings)
ai.model.typed_hint: The provider does not list this name. Use it only if you know the exact model name.

ai.nsfw.label: Adult content
ai.nsfw.info: This provider can generate adult content (NSFW), depending on the model. As long as the switch is off, OmniWrench instructs the assistant to stay work-safe. The provider's own rules always apply.
ai.nsfw.confirm:
Allow adult content for this assistant?

Confirm that you are of legal age and that this is permitted on this computer and in your organisation. The responsibility lies with you. The provider's rules still apply.
ai.nsfw.active: NSFW content is allowed for this assistant.

ai.note.use_minimax: Hailuo videos are available via the MiniMax entry.
ai.note.use_api: The chat subscription does not work in other programs. Please use the Mistral entry with an API key.
ai.edit.fill_url: Please replace the placeholder in the address (e.g. <ACCOUNT_ID>) with your own value.

ai.def.title: Assistant per function
ai.def.intro: Which assistant each AI tool uses by default, what it can do according to the last check and how much volume it reports. Changes here apply to the AI tools right away; a choice made in a tool is stored here as well.
ai.def.hint: Local options (💻) need no account. Whisper, Piper and Vosk are set up in the respective tool or when it is installed.
ai.ollama.title: Set up Ollama
ai.ollama.intro: Ollama runs language models entirely on this computer – free and without an account. Install and start it here and download models; then choose a model in the connection.
ai.ollama.stopped: Ollama is installed but not running.
ai.ollama.missing: Ollama is not installed on this computer.
ai.ollama.install_q: Install Ollama for the current user (winget or the official setup from ollama.com, about 1 GB, no administrator rights needed)?
ai.ollama.copied: Command copied. Run it in a terminal (needs sudo), then open this window again.
ai.ollama.delete_q: Delete the model {model} from this computer?
ai.ollama.hint: Rule of thumb: the model should fit into the graphics memory (or RAM) with some room to spare. Small models answer quickly, large ones handle functions and long texts better.
